stated: The Conservative Party will pass the UK's first ever Veterans' Bill to enshrine Veterans' rights in law, ensuring qualifications from service are recognized in civilian life, creating a legal duty on government to look after veterans, and widening the scope of the Armed Forces Covenant.

source.quote: We will pass the UK’s first ever Veterans’ Bill to enshrine Veterans’ rights in law. Ensuring qualifications from Service are correctly recognised in civilian life, creating a legal duty on government to look after our Veterans and widening the scope of the Armed Forces Covenant in law to include the UK Government and devolved administrations.

bearing_set.reason: Requiring civilian recognition of military qualifications directly improves veterans' employment prospects, job quality, and earning capacity in the labour market.

Creating a statutory duty on government to look after veterans and widening the Armed Forces Covenant scope would materially affect healthcare and mental-health access for a population with documented unmet needs.

A statutory duty on government to 'look after veterans' and an expanded Covenant creates enforceable obligations around social care and later-life support for veterans, bearing on social care access and security-against-poverty indicators in O8.

Ensuring qualifications from service are recognised in civilian life directly addresses skills recognition and opportunity, affecting veterans' ability to translate military training into civilian career pathways — squarely within the skills/opportunity indicator.

Enshrining veterans' rights in law and creating a legal duty not to disadvantage people because of their service is an equal-treatment protection, analogous in structure to anti-discrimination law — it creates enforceable legal status for a specific group against differential treatment.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: healthcare access (O3), skills and opportunity recognition (O7), and legal equal-treatment protections (O9). Effects on public finances (O12) and later-life security (O8) are plausible but too diffuse and unspecified in the policy to clear the non-negligible bar without more detail on scope and cost.
